title: Memory Networks
one_line_claim: Proposes an explicit, addressable long-term memory component read/written by a neural controller, separate from model parameters.

title: End-To-End Memory Networks
one_line_claim: Makes memory-network read/write fully differentiable and trainable end-to-end with weaker supervision than the original Memory Networks.

title: Neural Turing Machines
one_line_claim: Couples a neural controller to an external memory matrix via differentiable attention, enabling learned algorithms like copy and sort.

title: Hybrid computing using a neural network with dynamic external memory
one_line_claim: The Differentiable Neural Computer adds dynamic memory allocation and temporal link tracking, letting a network solve graph traversal and reasoning tasks that require variable-sized structured memory.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
one_line_claim: Combines a parametric seq2seq model with a non-parametric retriever over an external corpus so generation is grounded in retrieved documents rather than frozen weights alone.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
one_line_claim: Treats the LLM context window like virtual memory, using an OS-style paging scheme (self-directed function calls) to move information between a bounded context and external storage to give the illusion of unbounded memory.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
one_line_claim: Introduces a memory stream of observations plus a reflection mechanism that periodically synthesizes higher-level memories, retrieved and used to condition believable agent behavior.

title: Why there are complementary learning systems in the hippocampus and neocortex
one_line_claim: Argues the brain needs two learning systems — a fast hippocampal one for episodic recall and a slow neocortical one for structured, interleaved consolidation — to avoid catastrophic interference.

title: What Learning Systems do Intelligent Agents Need? Complementary Learning Systems Theory Updated
one_line_claim: Updates complementary learning systems theory in light of deep RL and episodic-memory findings, motivating fast/slow-learning-system architectures as a computational analogue of hippocampal-neocortical interaction.

title: Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks
one_line_claim: Elastic Weight Consolidation penalizes changes to parameters important for earlier tasks (via a Fisher-information-weighted quadratic penalty) to mitigate catastrophic forgetting during sequential training.

title: Test-Time Training with Self-Supervision for Generalization under Distribution Shifts
one_line_claim: Updates model parameters at test time via a self-supervised auxiliary task on each new input, adapting to distribution shift without labeled data.

title: Using Fast Weights to Attend to the Recent Past
one_line_claim: Introduces a fast-changing weight matrix, updated by a Hebbian-like rule from recent activity, that lets a network attend to its own recent history at a timescale between slow weights and short-term activity.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
one_line_claim: Freezes pretrained weights and injects trainable low-rank update matrices per layer, making targeted, cheap fine-tuning/adaptation of large models feasible without touching the full parameter set.

title: Transformers Learn In-Context by Gradient Descent
one_line_claim: Shows constructively that a transformer's forward pass over a prompt can implement steps of gradient descent on an implicit in-context loss, giving a mechanistic account of in-context learning.

title: Why Can GPT Learn In-Context? Language Models Implicitly Perform Gradient Descent as Meta-Optimizers
one_line_claim: Draws a formal duality between attention and gradient-descent-based finetuning, framing in-context learning as an implicit, weight-unchanging optimization process.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
one_line_claim: Has an agent verbally reflect on task feedback/failures and stores that reflection in an episodic memory buffer used to condition subsequent attempts, substituting for gradient-based RL updates.

title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
one_line_claim: Uses the same frozen LLM to generate output, critique it, and refine it iteratively in a feedback loop, with no parameter updates or external training signal.

title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
one_line_claim: Samples multiple diverse reasoning chains and marginalizes over them by majority vote on the final answer, improving reasoning accuracy without any self-correction step per se.

title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems
one_line_claim: Trains a separate verifier model to score candidate solutions and select among generator samples, offloading correctness-checking to a distinct learned model rather than the generator itself.

title: Let's Verify Step by Step
one_line_claim: Shows a process-level reward model, trained on human step-by-step correctness labels, outperforms outcome-level supervision for catching reasoning errors.

title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
one_line_claim: Finds that without external, ground-truth feedback, LLMs prompted to self-critique and revise their own reasoning frequently make correct answers worse, undercutting claims of intrinsic self-correction.

title: World Models
one_line_claim: Trains a compressed generative model of an environment (VAE + RNN) and evolves a small controller entirely inside that learned latent 'dream' simulation before transferring to the real environment.

title: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model
one_line_claim: MuZero learns a model of only the quantities relevant to planning (reward, value, policy) without reconstructing observations, and plans with MCTS purely in that learned latent model.

title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
one_line_claim: DreamerV3 learns a world model from experience and trains a policy purely from imagined rollouts inside it, achieving strong performance across many domains with one fixed set of hyperparameters.

title: Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination
one_line_claim: Backpropagates value gradients directly through imagined multi-step latent trajectories of a learned world model to learn behaviors efficiently, without interacting with the real environment.

title: The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory?
one_line_claim: Proposes that brains (and action) minimize variational free energy, unifying perception, learning, and action under a single generative-model / predictive-coding framework — active inference.

title: Learning to Represent Programs with Graphs
one_line_claim: Represents source code as a graph capturing syntax, control flow, and data flow, and applies gated graph neural networks to tasks like variable-misuse detection, giving a structural rather than purely textual code representation.

title: Modeling and Discovering Vulnerabilities with Code Property Graphs
one_line_claim: Introduces the code property graph, merging AST, control-flow graph, and program-dependence graph into one joint representation, queryable to discover vulnerability patterns across a codebase.

title: code2vec: Learning Distributed Representations of Code
one_line_claim: Represents a code snippet as a bag of AST paths and learns a distributed embedding that predicts semantic properties such as method names, giving a learned structural fingerprint of code.

title: Interprocedural Slicing Using Dependence Graphs
one_line_claim: Extends program dependence graphs across procedure boundaries to compute interprocedural slices, the structural basis for determining what code is affected by / affects a given statement.

title: A Survey of Program Slicing Techniques
one_line_claim: Surveys the family of static and dynamic program-slicing techniques used to identify the subset of a program that can influence (or is influenced by) a given point — a core building block of change-impact analysis.

title: The Program Dependence Graph and Its Use in Optimization
one_line_claim: Introduces the program dependence graph combining control and data dependence in one structure, the ancestor representation behind most modern static change-impact and slicing tools.
